component.name: Steam Library Mover
component.summary: Move installed Steam games between Steam libraries safely

description.p: Steam Library Mover relocates installed Steam games between Steam libraries without using Steam's own “Move install folder” operation. It copies the game, its app manifest, the Proton prefix, shader cache and Workshop data, verifies the destination, updates libraryfolders.vdf atomically, and only then removes the source.

It is designed for Linux libraries stored on NTFS or other Windows-compatible filesystems, where Proton prefixes can be corrupted by Windows-invalid filenames. The tool understands shared compatdata symlinks and never tries to move a Proton prefix onto itself.

Steam must be completely closed while a move runs. Games can be selected in batches, dragged onto a destination drive, paused and resumed. Every operation is journaled, can be inspected in the Recovery dialog, and is refused when the game is updating, a prefix is already in use, a destination conflict exists, or the filesystem cannot safely store the game. An optional backup mode keeps the source payload in hidden folders. Library Health finds stale locks, orphaned data and broken compatdata links, and can quarantine stale lock/temp files without deleting them. NTFS Doctor clearly reports whether each NTFS library already has a valid shared compatdata symlink. Reflink-capable filesystems use an instant, verified clone path. A compact layout, sortable columns, drive-type icons, staged progress with speed/ETA and light/dark themes are included.
The application is not affiliated with Valve Corporation. Steam is a trademark of Valve Corporation.

Speeds up transfer verification and copying: source hashes are captured during copy and reused for destination-only verification, files verify and copy concurrently where safe, sparse files keep their holes, and copy completion is atomic. The review dialog now supports per-game selection and fresh preflight checks, and the window remembers its layout.

Adds resume and automatic repair for interrupted copies, descriptor-relative deletion, a machine-wide lock, mid-copy process monitoring, asynchronous Steam shutdown, journal retention, and pinned release supply-chain tooling.
Fixes the NTFS acknowledgement bypass, revalidates disk state before and during the commit, adds recovery actions, and corrects verification, parser and pause/ETA edge cases.

Keeps an existing destination shader cache instead of blocking the move, clarifies that full verification is optional, explains why Start is disabled, and isolates GUI test settings from the user configuration.

Safety update: full checksum verification is now the default, rollback restores metadata before deleting data and validates journal paths, NTFS acknowledgement is enforced in the core, and release builds run the test suite.
Fixes test isolation so package checks succeed while Steam is running. No runtime behavior change.
Safety release: preserves relative symlinks exactly, fixes permanently unfinished journal states, guards rollback against root and running Steam/game processes, and centralizes version metadata.
Adds an Open on ProtonDB action to the game context menu for Proton and unknown-runtime games.
Adds the GitHub, AUR and issue-tracker links, plus the application version, to the About dialog.

Packaging and release automation update: AppImage, Arch package, Flatpak build artifact, AUR publishing workflow and README screenshots. The desktop application and move engine are unchanged from 0.1.0.
Initial development snapshot: journaled game moves, NTFS preflight checks, shared compatdata handling, CLI and Qt desktop UI.
